title: Coefficient criterion for powers of the combined power series ideal
statement: Let Λ be any commutative ring, J an ideal of Λ, and d,n nonnegative integers. In R=Λ[[X_1,...,X_d]] [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], put a=JR+(X_1,...,X_d). For every F in R, F belongs to a^n if and only if for every exponent E of total degree |E|<n its coefficient belongs to J^(n-|E|). No Noetherianity or completeness hypothesis is required.

source.place: Remark Tag 032C (uses completeness without proof); agent-formulated coefficient argument, steps 1--3 of lem-weil-pbc-power-series-complete-over-complete-base. Official remark read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/032C.

proof.text: For every n, define S_n by coeff_E(F) in J^(n-degree E) for all exponents E (truncated subtraction). Coefficientwise addition and the finite Cauchy product make S_n an ideal: in a product G*F each summand uses a coefficient of F of degree at most degree E. The same convolution proves S_m*S_n is contained in S_(m+n), since (m-degree A)+(n-degree B) is at least m+n-degree(A+B). Powers of J are antitone in their exponents. The constants from J and every variable lie in S_1. Induction gives a^n contained in S_n.

A monomial X^E belongs to the degree(E) power of the variables ideal: express it as the product of X_i^(E_i), use membership of X_i in the span, multiply the ideal powers, and sum the exponents. Suppose F has zero coefficients of degree below n. For each exponent E of degree at least n choose mu(E) <= E of degree n (Finsupp.exists_le_degree_eq); for other E put mu(E)=0. There are finitely many degree-n exponents M. Define G_M(B) to be coeff_(M+B)(F) when mu(M+B)=M and zero otherwise. Comparing coefficients gives F=sum_M X^M G_M: at a high-degree E exactly M=mu(E) contributes; at a low-degree E no degree-n M can divide E. Thus F lies in the nth power of the variables ideal. The choice only partitions a given explicit coefficient family and uses a proved existence theorem.

For F satisfying the low-degree coefficient conditions, form the finite sum low=sum_(degree E<n) coeff_E(F) X^E. Its coefficient at E is coeff_E(F) if degree E<n and zero otherwise. The tail F-low has zero coefficients below degree n, so the preceding step puts it in (X)^n, hence in a^n. Each low term is the product of its constant coefficient in the image of J^(n-degree E), hence in a^(n-degree E), with X^E in a^(degree E). Since degree E<n, these exponents add to n. Add the finite low part and its tail. For n=0 the low part is empty and the tail result is membership in the whole ring. For d=0 only E=0 exists; all arguments still apply.

proof_origin.place: Steps 1--3 of the parent coefficient proof, fully formalized by S1. Remark 032C only states the motivating complete-local-ring special cases.

mathlib_searches.query: Membership in a power of the ideal generated by a base ideal J and variables in multivariate formal power series is characterized by coefficients in J to the power n minus total degree
Membership in the nth power of the ideal generated by J and variables in multivariate power series is equivalent to each coefficient of degree less than n belonging to J to the power n minus degree

from.place: step 7 of its split (source: Lemma 0GS2, proof: the essential-surjectivity paragraphs); coefficient ideal powers in steps 1--3 of lem-weil-pbc-power-series-complete-over-complete-base

lean.statement: theorem power_series_mem_combined_ideal_pow_iff (Λ : Type u) [CommRing Λ] (J : Ideal Λ) (d n : ℕ) (F : MvPowerSeries (Fin d) Λ) : F ∈ (Ideal.map (algebraMap Λ (MvPowerSeries (Fin d) Λ)) J ⊔ Ideal.span (Set.range (MvPowerSeries.X : Fin d → MvPowerSeries (Fin d) Λ))) ^ n ↔ ∀ E : Fin d →₀ ℕ, E.degree < n → MvPowerSeries.coeff E F ∈ J ^ (n - E.degree)
